key_insight: For predicting welding properties, stacking ensembles achieved higher task-specific accuracy, while the multitask neural network provided strong shared-learning generalization across related outputs.
engineering_relevance: The study helps welding engineers choose between a unified multitask model for coupled property prediction and an ensemble approach when the highest accuracy for each weld metric is the priority.
method: Compared a multitask neural network (shared hidden layers + task-specific outputs) against stacking ensemble learning.
Predicted three welding targets: UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness.
Evaluated model performance using RMSE and R².
evidence_signal: Stacking ensemble achieved RMSE/R² of 0.0263/0.9863 for UTS, 0.0467/0.9782 for weld hardness, and 0.1109/0.8453 for HAZ hardness; MTNN achieved 0.1288/0.6724, 0.0886/0.9215, and 0.1125/0.8407, respectively.
watch_item: Results are based on a shared dataset, so model choice may depend on dataset size, task correlation, and whether deployment needs a single multioutput model or separate high-accuracy predictors.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
